title: Opening
text: Clubs generate huge amounts of match video, but turning that footage into reliable, structured information is still hard. This is a football intelligence platform for AZ Alkmaar: a pipeline that takes raw match video and turns it into validated, structured football data, and eventually, football intelligence you can act on.

title: Segmentation principle
text: We don't ask an AI model to watch an entire ninety minute match and guess what happened. Instead, the platform divides video into controlled, thirty to sixty second segments. Each segment is small enough to trace, test, and validate independently, the discipline that turns a demo trick into an engineering pipeline you can actually trust.

title: Segment builder
text: Here is the segment builder, running against real Alfheim match footage. An operator selects a starting point and duration, and the platform prepares a playable window, this one, fifteen to sixteen minutes into the match. Behind the scenes it extracts frames, caches detections, and prepares everything the analysis pipeline needs. Segments can be grouped, replayed, and reprocessed independently, so every result traces back to an exact, reproducible slice of video.

title: AI event detection
text: Inside each segment, computer vision detects players, the ball, and team shape, and proposes candidate football events, passes, turnovers, shots, fouls, each with a timestamp, a team, and a confidence score. But a raw AI prediction is a proposal, not a fact. Every candidate still has to earn its place in the statistics by passing through football rules validation. That principle sits underneath everything else you'll see: predictions get questioned, never assumed.

title: Rules Reviewer and passed gate
text: This is the Global Football Rules Reviewer. Every candidate event is checked against the actual I-FAB Laws of the Game and the project's own analytics definitions, then independently reconstructed from the video before it's compared to the engine's output. In this fifteen to sixteen minute segment, fifteen proposals were reviewed. Fourteen ended up matching confirmed engine events exactly, most lined up directly, and one engine event was independently verified after its proposal didn't correspond to it. The one remaining proposal that didn't match a distinct engine event was excluded from the published statistics, and match state annotations stayed out of the numbers too. All one hundred and five protected regression tests passed before this segment was published and locked.

title: Statistics and maturity
text: Only validated events feed the statistics layer. Possession, passes, pass completion, fouls, and interceptions are implemented and undergoing thorough validation. Shots and shots on target are currently in review. Corners are near completion. Offsides, attacking and defensive actions, and player, team, and formation statistics are still in development. We would rather show you exactly where each statistic stands than call everything finished.

title: Copilot over validated data
text: Once data is validated, Copilot can reason over it directly, how many passes were completed, how sure are we, what still needs review. Because it is answering from validated structured events rather than raw predictions, the insight is only as reliable as the validation behind it. That is exactly the point.

title: Future vision and Xebia
text: The same architecture can extend to tactical patterns, scouting, and player development, including post processed views like player heat maps, pitch zone identification, and shot placement and attribution by player, built from the full recorded clip rather than the live statistics screen. It can also run in a private, on premises environment where that's required, including a future concept where a main camera queries neighbouring goal end and touchline cameras for a second opinion when its own confidence is low, all on local infrastructure rather than the cloud. This prototype was built by a focused team to prove the concept quickly. If AZ wants to take it further, Xebia Netherlands can bring additional AI and engineering capacity to scale the next phase.
